questions.question: 1. What is a 'cell cluster' in a cellular network?

answers.a: A group of users all connected to the same cell tower.
answers.b: A single, oversized cell used to cover a large rural area.
answers.c: A group of adjacent cells where the entire set of available frequencies is used exactly once.
answers.d: All the cells in a network that belong to the same service provider.

questions.question: 2. What is the main advantage of using a **small** cluster size?

answers.b: It increases the total system capacity.
answers.c: It simplifies the handoff process between cells.
answers.d: It allows for a much larger frequency reuse distance.

questions.question: 3. What is the main advantage of using a **large** cluster size?

answers.a: It increases the number of channels available in each cell.
answers.b: It allows for a greater number of total users in the system.
answers.c: It increases the distance between co-channel cells, reducing interference.
answers.d: It makes the cell towers cheaper to build.

questions.question: 4. If a cellular system has a large cluster size, what does this imply for each individual cell within that cluster?

answers.a: Each cell will have a larger number of frequency channels.
answers.b: Each cell will have a smaller number of frequency channels.
answers.c: Each cell will experience more co-channel interference.
answers.d: Each cell must be physically larger.

questions.question: 5. How are cell clusters used to provide coverage over a large geographic area?

answers.a: A single, massive cluster is created to cover the entire area.
answers.b: The cluster pattern is repeated, or tessellated, over and over.
answers.c: The cluster size is continuously changed to fit the population.
answers.d: Clusters are only used for the initial network setup.

questions.question: 6. What is the primary trade-off when designing a cell cluster size?

answers.a: Signal strength versus the cost of the base station.
answers.c: Data speed versus the number of voice calls.
answers.d: Coverage area versus battery life of mobile phones.

questions.question: 7. How does increasing the cluster size affect co-channel interference?

answers.c: It has no effect on co-channel interference.

questions.question: 8. How does decreasing the cluster size affect the overall system capacity?

answers.c: It has no effect on system capacity.
answers.d: It makes the system capacity unstable.

questions.question: 9. The set of all available frequencies for the system is allocated...

answers.a: to every single cell in the network.
answers.b: to a single cluster, which is then repeated.
answers.c: to only the cells on the edge of the network.
answers.d: to only one cell in the very center of the network.

questions.question: 10. What happens to the physical distance between co-channel cells when the cluster size is made larger?

answers.c: The distance stays exactly the same.
answers.d: The co-channel cells are moved next to each other.
